To find which two consecutive whole numbers $\sqrt{110}$ lies between, we first identify the perfect squares that are just below and just above $110.$

The perfect squares closest to $110$ are $100$ and $121.$ We have

$$
100<110<121.
$$

Taking the square root of each number, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\sqrt{100} & <\sqrt{110}<\sqrt{121} \\ 10 & <\sqrt{110}<11.\end{aligned}
$$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14185481/assets/9bef06cb0000173c30147f4f9f633f3adec207b688adb005bcf0fff1aa8d7b13.png)

This means that $\sqrt{110}$ lies between the consecutive whole numbers $10$ and $11.$ 

Therefore, since $a<b,$ we have $a=10$ and $b=11.$
